adds.title: Neuer MANEO-Report: Erneut über 700 LSBTIQ+ -feindliche Übergriffe in Berlin registriert – MANEO
adds.summary: MANEO, Berlin's anti-violence documentation project, states that it recorded 723 LSBTIQ+-hostile incidents in Berlin in 2025, slightly fewer than the 738 documented in 2024, from 1,014 new reports - a new high; its 12 May 2026 release lists insults, threats and physical attacks in public transport, parks and streets, with Schöneberg, Neukölln, Kreuzberg, Friedrichshain and Tiergarten most affected, plus 58 attacks on LSBTIQ+ venues, memorials and events. MANEO says the figures capture only part of reality because of a high dark figure, and that the counselling centre itself was attacked several times in 2025. This is the primary Berlin project behind the record's claim that documented homophobic violence in the capital is rising, and it names Neukölln - the record's café-owner example - among the worst-hit districts.

adds.title: MANEO erschüttert über Anschlag beim Berliner CSD – Solidarität mit den Verletzten – MANEO
adds.summary: MANEO reports that at the 48th Berlin Christopher Street Day a vehicle drove into a crowd in the Tiergarten area, killing one woman, injuring several people and forcing the event to be cancelled; the project offers victim counselling and an anonymous reporting line (030-2163336, daily 17:00-19:00). This is a dated, outcome-specific Berlin Pride incident - evidence that the serious attack risk the record's 2025 'be vigilant' organisers warned about has materialised at the capital's own CSD.

adds.title: trans*, inter* und nicht-binäre Personen in Haft - Berlin.de
adds.summary: The Berlin state government's official prison-service page states that legislation has created a basis for considering trans, inter* and non-binary people held in custody, that Berlin prison staff are responsible for taking each detainee's individual needs into account within the legal framework, and it details gender-segregated placement, intake procedures and counselling and support offers. This is Berlin-specific official information on how the capital's prison administration (JVA Moabit, JVA für Frauen Berlin, etc.) treats trans/inter/non-binary detainees, the detention-side counterpart to the city's anti-queer violence statistics.

adds.title: Deutlich mehr queerfeindliche Straftaten in Hessen | hessenschau.de
adds.summary: hessenschau reports (21 August 2025) that the Hessian interior ministry's answer to a Landtag inquiry by three Grüne MPs recorded 135 queer-hostile offences in Hessen in 2024, 52 more than the previous year, among them 16 cases of dangerous grievous bodily harm, seven of bodily harm, 13 of property damage and 26 of insult, with many victims not reporting so that a high dark figure is assumed. Interior Minister Roman Poseck (CDU) called the development 'alarmierend', attributed part of the responsibility to far-right forces, and the ministry counted suspects identified in 46 of the 2024 proceedings and six convictions. This is the media confirmation of the record's police-registered 33 (2022) to 83 (2023) to 135 (2024) series.

adds.title: Queerfeindliche Straftaten in Hessen vervierfacht: "Nur die Spitze des Eisbergs" | hessenschau.de
adds.summary: hessenschau reports (17 May 2026) from a further Poseck answer to a Grüne Landtag inquiry that Hessen police counted 141 queer-hostile offences in 2025, against 83 in 2023 and 33 in 2022 - a more than fourfold rise within four years that Poseck called 'alarmierend' and only 'the tip of the iceberg' given the high dark figure; he cited a January 2026 Kassel tram incident in which a male couple was homophobically insulted, threatened and spat on. The article notes Hessen police keep dedicated contact officers for this hate crime and the state government promises consistent prosecution. It updates the record's statistics with the 2025 figure of 141 and confirms the state's own alarm at the trend.

adds.title: BASHKKA files legal complaint against Frankfurt Airport for discrimination · News
adds.summary: Resident Advisor reports (20 June 2025) that trans woman artist BASHKKA filed a legal complaint under Germany's Equal Treatment Act after a male security officer refused her a search by a female officer during screening at Frankfurt Airport on 23 November 2024 and told her she was 'not a woman'; Frankfurt Airport later apologised by email, said the security service provider had been instructed to investigate, and promised security staff would be trained on dealing with transgender and gender non-conforming travellers. This is a dated, jurisdiction-specific case of transphobic treatment at Hessen's main international airport - the first screening-gate incident evidence for this record.

adds.title: German controversy surrounds jail term for transgender far-right extremist - BBC News
adds.summary: BBC News reports (20 August 2025) that Marla-Svenja Liebich, then Sven Liebich, was sentenced in July 2023 by the Halle District Court in Saxony-Anhalt to one year and six months' imprisonment without parole for incitement to hatred, defamation and insult, and changed her legal gender from male to female by declaration at a registry office under Germany's Self-Determination Act at the end of 2024. The article records the ensuing controversy - the chief public prosecutor in Halle told MDR Saxony-Anhalt that Liebich would begin the term at Chemnitz women's prison, while German outlets including Der Spiegel questioned the change's seriousness - and notes Liebich also lost a case against journalist Julian Reichelt at Berlin Regional Court. This grounds in Saxony-Anhalt the 'Fall Liebich' that the record identifies as the trigger for its Bundesrat initiative.

adds.title: Germany: Gender switch neo-Nazi sent to men's prison - DW
adds.summary: DW reports (16 July 2026) that Marla-Svenja Liebich, legally registered as a woman since 2025, was transferred to a men's prison (Zeithain, Meissen district) after being extradited from the Czech Republic, with prison management saying the decision prioritised the safety of women at the Chemnitz facility. It recalls that Liebich was sentenced to 18 months in July 2023, organised far-right demonstrations since 2014 including many on Halle's central market square, was arrested in the Czech Republic in April 2026, and that a court has yet to decide whether the changes can be reversed. This documents the outcome of the Saxony-Anhalt-linked case behind the record's initiative, including the still-open question of reversing SBGG-based changes.
